items.title: Tarlatamab-Durvalumab Maintenance for Extensive-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer
items.authors: Pérol M, Yoshida T, Ahn MJ, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer have poor outcomes, with a median overall survival of approximately 12 to 13 months. Tarlatamab (a bispecific T-cell engager targeting delta-like ligand 3 [DLL3] and CD3) was previously shown to improve survival as second-line therapy. Whether adding tarlatamab to durvalumab (an anti-programmed death ligand 1 agent) after initial chemoimmunotherapy could significantly improve survival in the context of maintenance therapy after first remission has been unclear. Methods: In this phase 3, international, open-label, randomized trial, we compared tarlatamab-durvalumab with durvalumab as first-line maintenance therapy in patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer without progression after initial chemoimmunotherapy. Overall survival and progression-free survival were assessed from randomization at the start of maintenance therapy as the primary and key secondary end points, respectively. Results of the prespecified interim analysis (data-cutoff date, July 7, 2026) are reported here. Results: A total of 563 patients were randomly assigned to receive tarlatamab-durvalumab (282 patients) or durvalumab (281 patients). At a median follow-up of 15.9 months in the tarlatamab-durvalumab group and 16.1 months in the durvalumab group, the estimated median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 20.8 to could not be estimated) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 12.7 months (95% CI, 11.2 to 14.8) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for death, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.54; P<0.001). The median progression-free survival was 7.4 months (95% CI, 5.6 to 9.1) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 1.9 months (95% CI, 1.9 to 2.0) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.42; P<0.001). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 46.8% of the patients who received tarlatamab-durvalumab and in 40.6% of those who received durvalumab alone. Cytokine release syndrome, mainly of grade 1 or 2, was seen in nearly half the patients receiving tarlatamab-durvalumab. Conclusions: Tarlatamab-durvalumab maintenance therapy resulted in significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival than durvalumab alone among patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. (Funded by Amgen and AstraZeneca; DeLLphi-305 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06211036.).

items.title: Durvalumab, Tremelimumab, and Enfortumab Vedotin in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer
items.authors: Powles T, Grande E, Simone G, et al.
items.abstract: Background: The standard of care for patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer continues to evolve. Whether perioperative durvalumab, with or without tremelimumab, plus neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin is effective in such patients is unknown. Methods: In this phase 3 open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1:1 ratio, patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based chemotherapy to receive neoadjuvant durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin every 3 weeks for three cycles, followed by radical cystectomy and then adjuvant durvalumab every 4 weeks for nine cycles; neoadjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (tremelimumab for two cycles only), radical cystectomy, and adjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab (tremelimumab for one cycle only); or radical cystectomy alone (control). The dual primary end points were event-free survival in each of the two durvalumab groups as compared with that in the control group. The two durvalumab groups were not compared with each other. The key secondary end point was overall survival. Results: In total, 233 patients were assigned to the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group, 233 to the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group, and 229 to the control group. Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 63.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 56.5 to 69.7) with durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin and 45.1% (95% CI, 38.2 to 51.8) with control (hazard ratio for an event or death, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.38 to 0.67; P<0.001); estimated overall survival at 24 months was 78.4% and 69.4%, respectively (hazard ratio for death, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.40 to 0.83; P = 0.003). Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 60.1% (95% CI, 53.2 to 66.2) with durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (hazard ratio for an event or death vs. control, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 71.1% of patients in the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group (treatment-related, 30.7%), in 79.5% of those in the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group (treatment-related, 44.5%), and in 50.2% of those in the control group. Conclusions: Perioperative durvalumab with or without tremelimumab plus three cycles of neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin resulted in significantly better event-free survival outcomes than surgery alone. Perioperative durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin led to significantly better overall survival outcomes than surgery alone. Grade 3 or higher adverse events of any cause were noted in more than half the patients in the durvalumab groups.…

items.title: Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus treatment of physician's choice in previously treated endometrial cancer (TroFuse-005/ENGOT-en23/GOG-3095): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial
items.authors: Lorusso D, Martin-Babau J, Backes F, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Therapeutic options for patients with endometrial cancer who progress after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy are scarce, and prognosis is poor. Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) is a trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2-directed antibody-drug conjugate with a unique, bifunctional linker that maximises delivery of a belotecan-derived topoisomerase I inhibitor payload to tumour cells. This study aimed to compare sac-TMT with the treatment of physician's choice (TPC) in patients with endometrial cancer who had been previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. Methods: In this randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial, patients were recruited from 242 gynaecological oncology centres across 31 countries and regions. Participating centres were selected based on established expertise in gynaecological oncology and an adequate volume of potentially eligible patients. Eligible patients were female and aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma or carcinosarcoma, who had received up to three previous lines of therapy, including systemic platinum-based chemotherapy and anti-programmed death 1 or anti-programmed death ligand 1 therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) via central interactive response technology to receive intravenous sac-TMT (4 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle) or TPC (intravenous doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or intravenous paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle). Investigators and patients were not masked to treatment; radiologists performing blinded independent central review were fully masked. Randomisation was stratified by mismatch repair status (deficient vs proficient), trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 expression by immunohistochemistry (TROP2 EPR20043 Formulation Locked Assay [Roche Tissue Diagnostics, Tucson, AZ, USA]; low [0% to <50% of tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity] vs medium-high [≥50% tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity]), number of previous lines of systemic therapy (≤2 vs 3), and baseline disease status per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) by blinded independent central review (measurable vs non-measurable). Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) assessed by blinded independent central review and overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population. items.title: First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial
items.authors: Slomovitz BM, Zhu J, Yin R, et al.
items.abstract: Background: A need exists for first-line chemotherapy-free options in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. We therefore assessed the efficacy, quality of life, and safety of first-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. Methods: The KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15 multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial was conducted at 122 centres in 24 countries in the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Adult participants (≥18 years) with inoperable, stage III or IV, persistent, advanced, or recurrent dMMR endometrial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 cycles or intravenous carboplatin area under the curve 5 mg/mL or 6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for six cycles. Randomisation was stratified by disease status, histology, and previous receipt of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival per RECIST version 1.1, by blinded independent central review, and overall survival. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05173987, and is ongoing. Findings: Between Feb 22, 2022, and Dec 12, 2023, 299 participants were assigned to pembrolizumab (n=149) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (n=150). At the cutoff for the prespecified interim analysis in the intention-to-treat population (April 24, 2026), median progression-free survival was 38·2 months (95% CI 17·9 months-not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 8·4 months (6·8-10·4) in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·57, 95% CI 0·42-0·79; p=0·0002). Estimated progression-free survival was 75% (95% CI 67-81) versus 76% (68-82) at 6 months, 67% (59-74) versus 40% (32-48) at 12 months, and 53% (44-61) versus 30% (22-38) at 36 months. The prespecified statistical significance criterion for overall survival was not met at the interim analysis (medians not reached; HR 0·77, 95% CI 0·52-1·15; p=0·10). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27 (18%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 73 (51%) of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group.…

items.title: Management of Patients with High-risk Localised, Locally Advanced, and Biochemically Recurrent Prostate Cancer: Report from the 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference
items.authors: Gillessen S, Turco F, Davis ID, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Innovations have improved outcomes in high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (PC), yet high-level evidence remains limited for many management decisions. The 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference (APCCC) surveyed an international panel on key clinical questions to complement evidence-based guidelines. Objective: Here we present the voting results for the questions on high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent PC from APCCC 2026. Design, Setting, And Participants: Before the conference, a multidisciplinary panel of 144 international PC experts used a modified Delphi process to develop 313 multiple-choice consensus questions, of which 134 covered high-risk localised and locally advanced PC, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA) persistence and PSA recurrence, and side effects of treatment. These questions were administered to the 133 voting panel members "panellists" via a web-based survey prior to the conference. Outcome Measurements And Statistical Analysis: Consensus was defined a priori as ≥75% agreement, with strong consensus defined as ≥90% agreement. Overall, consensus was reached for 44 of the 134 questions (32.8%), with seven questions reaching a strong consensus. Results and limitations The voting results show varying degrees of consensus, as discussed in this article and as detailed in the Supplementary Material. An interactive heat map for the questions can be found at https://apccc.org/APCCC2026-votings-localised-and-locally-advanced-prostate-cancer/. These findings do not include a formal literature review or meta-analysis. Conclusions: The voting results can help physicians and patients navigate controversial areas of clinical management for which evidence is scant or conflicting. The findings can also help funders and policymakers in prioritising areas for future research. Importantly, APCCC 2026 once again identified important gaps (areas of no consensus) that merit evaluation in specifically designed trials.

items.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant (castration-resistant) prostate cancer (TALAPRO-2): a biomarker analysis of circulating tumour DNA and cells for prognosis and molecular profiling
items.authors: Yip SM, Laird AD, Agarwal N, et al.
items.abstract: Background: The TALAPRO-2 trial showed improved radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival with first-line talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (APMR; also referred to as castration-resistant prostate cancer) unselected for homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations treated. We aimed to assess HRR gene alteration status agreement between prospective solid tumour tissue and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) testing, the potential complementary value of prospective and retrospective ctDNA testing, and the prognostic utility of baseline ctDNA burden, changes in ctDNA burden, and circulating tumour cell (CTC) reductions. Methods: In TALAPRO-2, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, men aged 18 years or older (≥20 years in Japan) with asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic metastatic APMR prostate cancer and no previous life-prolonging systemic therapy for APMR disease were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive once daily, oral talazoparib 0·5 mg plus enzalutamide 160 mg or placebo plus enzalutamide and stratified by HRR gene alteration status and previous treatment for androgen pathway modulator-naive/sensitive disease. The sponsor, patients, and investigators were masked to allocation of talazoparib or placebo; enzalutamide was open label. In this exploratory analysis, HRR gene alteration status agreement was evaluated in the unselected intention-to-treat cohort between solid tumour tissue prospectively tested using a clinical trial assay based on FoundationOne CDx and retrospectively tested ctDNA samples, collected at screening and assessed using an assay based on FoundationOne Liquid CDx. Tumour burden was categorised as positive or negative (ctDNA tumour fraction detectable or not detectable). Reductions in CTCs, enumerated using CELLSEARCH, were defined as conversion (from five or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to four or fewer cells per 7·5 mL of blood) or CTC0 (from one or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to zero). Radiographic progression-free survival was assessed for patients with baseline ctDNA positivity (positive vs negative) and for patients with ctDNA conversion and CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 (and week 17 for CTC conversion and CTC0) by treatment group. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrial.gov, NCT03395197 and is active, not recruiting.…

items.title: A Randomized Trial of Multimodal Prehabilitation Before Robotic-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy to Improve Postoperative Quality of Life and Functional Outcomes
items.authors: Carbonell E, Dana F, Tena B, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) causes postoperative impairments. Although prehabilitation has shown benefits in surgical populations, data specific to RARP remain limited. We evaluated whether multimodal prehabilitation improves early postoperative health-related quality of life (HRQoL), functional recovery and mental health. Materials And Methods: Prospective, single-center randomized trial including men with prostate cancer scheduled for RARP (May 2022- September 2024). Participants were randomized to a 4-week multimodal prehabilitation program including physical and pelvic floor muscle training, nutritional counselling and psychological support or to usual care. The primary outcome was change in the EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status score from baseline to 1 month after surgery. Secondary endpoints included functional and perioperative outcomes at 1, 3 and 6 months. Results: Ninety-five of 100 randomized patients were analyzed (53 prehabilitation, 42 control). At 1-month post-operatively, global health status score was higher in the prehabilitation group (adjusted mean difference +15 points, 0-100 scale; 95% confidence interval (CI) 7-22; p<0.001). Improvements at 1-month were also observed in several HRQoL domains, mental health and urinary continence (mean difference in ICIQ-UI SF -2.7; p=0.032). No differences were detected in physical performance or erectile function. Prehabilitation benefits attenuated over time, with the global health status difference decreasing to +4.5 points at 6 months (-1.9 points/month; p = 0.024), whereas improvements in selected HRQoL domains, mental health, and ICIQ-UI SF were maintained throughout follow-up. Conclusions: Multimodal prehabilitation before RARP is feasible and should be integrated into clinical practice, as it enhances postoperative recovery and patient-centered outcomes.

items.title: FGFR Alterations in Bladder Cancer-From Molecular Pathogenesis to Precision Oncology
items.authors: Collins K, Cheng L
items.abstract: Importance: Alterations in the fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) pathway, particularly FGFR3, are among the most common genomic events in urothelial carcinoma (UC) and represent a cornerstone of precision oncology. Although FGFR3 alterations predominate, selected FGFR2 fusions also identify patients who may benefit from targeted therapy. This review summarizes the biology, molecular diagnostics, and evolving clinical applications of FGFR alterations in UC. Observations: FGFR2/3 alterations are clinically actionable biomarkers across non-muscle-invasive, muscle-invasive, metastatic, and upper-tract UC. Comprehensive genomic profiling, tissue sequencing, plasma circulating tumor DNA, urine-based molecular assays, and molecular residual disease assessment are expanding their roles in diagnosis, treatment selection, surveillance, and disease monitoring. Recent clinical studies support combination strategies, next-generation FGFR inhibitors, and earlier use of FGFR-directed therapy, while emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence-assisted pathology and integrated multi-omic biomarkers, may further improve patient selection. Conclusions And Relevance: FGFR alterations have become integral to the molecular classification and precision management of UC. Continued advances in molecular diagnostics, liquid biopsy, biomarker-guided therapy, and next-generation FGFR inhibitors are expected to further personalize care. This review provides a practical framework for integrating FGFR biomarkers into contemporary management and highlights emerging developments likely to influence future clinical practice.

items.title: Dosimetric impact of CBCT-guided online adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy for prostate cancer: a 250-fraction retrospective analysis
items.authors: Eldib A, Clark AT, Panetta J, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: To quantitatively evaluate the dosimetric benefit of CBCT-guided online adaptive radiotherapy (ART) for prostate SBRT compared with non-adaptive treatment planning, with emphasis on target coverage preservation and organ-at-risk (OAR) sparing. Methods And Materials: Fifty prostate patients treated on the Varian Ethos platform were retrospectively analyzed. For each fraction, scheduled plans (reference plan recalculated on daily anatomy) were compared with adapted plans (daily reoptimized plans). Target coverage was assessed using PTV D95% while bladder and rectal metrics were evaluated using institutional constraints. Fraction-level paired comparisons used the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Fractions with substantial scheduled-plan under-coverage (PTV D95% ≤80%) underwent cumulative dose reconstruction. Results: Adaptive plans achieved higher target coverage than scheduled plans (p < 0.001), although scheduled plans remained within ∼3% of prescription in 83% of fractions. Scheduled plans demonstrated a 20% reduction in PTV D95% in 3.6% of fractions and >5% coverage reduction in 11%, whereas no adaptive fractions showed similarly large deviations. Cumulative scheduled-only dose remained near prescription for most affected patients, with only one patient demonstrating a cumulative D95% reduction of ∼5%. OAR differences were small overall, with ART planning mainly reducing occasional constraint violations. Strict application of planning objectives resulted in 234 adaptive fractions meeting goals versus 62 scheduled fractions, improving to 135 with offline renormalization. Conclusions: CBCT-guided ART for prostate SBRT primarily improves robustness against infrequent but clinically significant dosimetric deviations rather than providing consistent superiority across most fractions.

items.title: Survival outcomes of treatment strategies for cTanyN3M0 esophageal cancer: A nationwide population-based study
items.authors: Hafkamp CJH, Geijsen ED, van Laarhoven HWM, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Patients with cTanyN3M0 esophageal cancer have a poor prognosis, due to a high risk of distant progression. Evidence on treatment outcomes for this subgroup is limited. This population-based study compared overall survival (OS) after treatment for cTanyN3M0 esophageal cancer. Methods: Patients diagnosed with cTanyN3M0 esophageal cancer 2015-2022 were identified from the Netherlands Cancer Registry. Eligible patients received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy intended for subsequent esophagectomy (nCRT), definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT), perioperative chemotherapy (pCT) or palliative therapy. OS was compared across groups and separately between nCRT and dCRT after propensity score-matching. Recurrence patterns were evaluated for 2015-2018. Results: Among 19,867 esophageal cancer patients, 316 were cTanyN3M0 and 265 met the inclusion criteria. Treatment groups were nCRT (n = 134, 51 %), dCRT (n = 59, 22 %), pCT (n = 11, 4 %) and palliative therapy (n = 61, 23 %). Esophagectomy was performed in 68.6 % after nCRT and 5.1 % after dCRT. Adjuvant nivolumab was given in 10.4 % after nCRT and 1.7 % after dCRT. Median OS for nCRT versus dCRT was 18.8 versus 15.2 months (hazard ratio [HR] 0.76, 95 % confidence interval [CI]: 0.54-1.08). After matching, median OS was 17.6 versus 16.1 months (38 patients per group; HR 0.78, 95 % CI: 0.46-1.31). Median OS after pCT was 18.9 months and after palliative therapy 7.1 months. Among 65 documented first recurrences, 85 % involved distant metastases. Conclusion: This real-world study on cTanyN3M0 esophageal cancer observed no statistically significant survival difference between nCRT and dCRT and a high risk of distant recurrence. These findings suggest that emphasis should be placed on improving systemic control.

items.title: Eltrombopag during induction chemotherapy in older patients with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia is safe and reduces platelet transfusion requirements: The EPAG-2015 French Innovative Leukemia Organization phase 2 randomized trial
items.authors: Pigneux A, Dumas PY, Bernard M, et al.
items.abstract: Abstract Background Elderly patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) treated with intensive chemotherapy are at risk of developing thrombopenia, which requires platelet transfusions. It would be interesting to provide them with thrombopoietin receptor agonists such as eltrombopag. Methods The EPAG‐2015 multicenter phase 2 trial (18 French hospitals from October 2018 to June 2021) blindly randomized elderly patients (aged ≥60 years) with placebo or eltrombopag administered on Day 11 after induction chemotherapy and continued until AML response evaluation (Day 45) or a platelet count of >100 × 109/L. A cohort of 110 patients with a median age of 70 years was included and randomized (55 per arm) to receive placebo or eltrombopag. Results After induction, 90 patients (81.8%) achieved complete response (CR) or CR with incomplete reconstitution (CRi) (45 in each group), including 74 patients with CR (38 with eltrombopag and 36 with placebo). With a median follow‐up for alive patients of 20.9 months the primary objective was not reached, given that there was no difference in overall survival (hazard ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 0.65–3.89; p = .31). Eltrombopag, however, did not lead to increased grade 3/4 adverse events, and was associated with a lower median number of platelet transfusions (eight; interquartile range [IQR], 6–14; vs. 10; IQR, 7–14; i.e., a 20% benefit). Conclusions This study failed to demonstrate a survival advantage after eltrombopag addition, at variance with previous reports, but shows that initiating eltrombopag after chemotherapy washout is feasible and safe, and resulted in a decreased need for platelet transfusions.

items.title: AAPM Medical Physics Practice Guideline 18.a: Superficial radiation therapy using low-energy kilovoltage x-rays
items.authors: Lee YC, Lim SB, Mondalek PM, et al.
items.abstract: Superficial radiation therapy (SRT), utilizing low-energy kilovoltage (kV) x-rays typically in the 50-100 kVp range, is a well-established modality in dermatology and radiation oncology clinics for the management of non-melanoma skin cancer and various benign dermatological conditions. The comprehensive medical physics practice guidelines presented in this report are designed to facilitate adherence to minimum standards for SRT delivery. A technical overview of commercially available SRT systems in the United States is provided. Detailed guidelines for commissioning and routine quality assurance are presented, specifying daily, monthly, and annual tests, alongside established action limits. The SRT clinical workflow is delineated, encompassing patient simulation, treatment time or monitor unit calculations, data entry, independent treatment plan review, and radiation delivery. A summary of typical state regulatory requirements for x-ray machines is included. Adherence to relevant state regulations is emphasized and radiation safety considerations, comprising structural shielding, radiation surveys, personnel monitoring, signage, periodic spot checks, and machine operation, are discussed to ensure a safe and effective clinical environment. References to relevant societal practice guidance are provided to support standardized clinical implementation.

items.title: Decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide versus busulfan-cyclophosphamide myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for reducing risk of relapse in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia in China: an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 3 trial
items.authors: Hu Z, Fan Z, Dai M, et al.
items.abstract: Background: An unmet need persists for optimal myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia. We investigated whether decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide (DAC-BuCy) conditioning reduced the risk of relapse compared with busulfan-cyclophosphamide (BuCy) conditioning. Methods: In this open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial at eight transplantation centres in China, eligible patients were aged 14-65 years, had morphologically confirmed KMT2A-rearranged leukaemia, and had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-2. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) before HSCT to DAC-BuCy (intravenous decitabine 20 mg/m2 once a day on days -14 to -10, intravenous busulfan 3·2 mg/kg once a day on days -7 to -4, and intravenous cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg once a day on days -3 to -2) or BuCy (same dose and duration of busulfan and cyclophosphamide). Randomisation was done with permuted blocks (block size four) with no stratification and was implemented through an independent, interactive, web-based response system. The primary endpoint was 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse in the intention-to-treat population. Safety was assessed in all patients who received treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03596892) and is complete. Findings: Between May 1, 2019, and Jan 31, 2023, 130 patients were randomised to receive a DAC-BuCy (n=65; 34 [52%] female and 31 [48%] male) or BuCy (n=65; 29 [45%] female and 36 [55%] male) regimen. Median follow-up was 34·7 months (IQR 30·2-52·5). 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 12% (95% CI 6-22) in the DAC-BuCy group and 29% (19-41) in the BuCy group (hazard ratio 0·41 [0·20-0·87]; p=0·017). The most common grade 3-5 adverse events were infections or infestations (DAC-BuCy group 27 [42%] and BuCy group 25 [38%]), acute graft-versus-host disease (DAC-BuCy group 23 [35%] and BuCy group 22 [34%]), and gastrointestinal disorders (DAC-BuCy group 14 [22%] and BuCy group 15 [23%]). Four (6%) patients in the DAC-BuCy group and five (8%) patients in the BuCy group died from adverse events, of which two were due to regimen-related toxicities: one nervous system disorder in the DAC-BuCy group and one cardiac disorder in the BuCy group. Interpretation: The addition of decitabine to BuCy conditioning reduced the risk of relapse with an acceptable safety profile in adult patients with KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia and could be a suitable therapeutic option for this population.…

items.title: Automation Bias in Large Language Model-Assisted Diagnostic Reasoning among Physicians Trained in AI Literacy - A Randomized Clinical Trial
items.authors: Qazi IA, Ali A, Khawaja AU, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Large language models (LLMs) have the potential to improve clinical reasoning, but can also hallucinate, generating plausible but false information that risks patient harm. This risk is amplified by automation bias, the tendency to over-rely on automated outputs. It remains unclear whether physicians formally trained to critically evaluate artificial intelligence (AI) outputs remain susceptible to this bias when LLM consultation is discretionary. Methods: We conducted a single-blind, randomized clinical trial from June 20 to August 15, 2025, involving 44 physicians in Pakistan who completed a 20-hour AI literacy training program. Post training, participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to diagnose six clinical vignettes. The control group received error-free diagnostic suggestions from Chat Generative Pretrained Transformer (ChatGPT) 4o, while the treatment group received suggestions containing deliberately introduced errors for three of the six cases, which were randomly ordered to minimize anchoring bias. Physicians could voluntarily consult ChatGPT-4o's recommendations alongside standard diagnostic resources, while retaining full autonomy to accept, modify, or reject its suggestions. The primary outcome was composite diagnostic reasoning accuracy (correct differentials, supporting or opposing evidence, top-choice diagnosis, and next steps) adjudicated by three blinded physicians; the secondary outcome was top-choice diagnosis accuracy. Results: Forty-four physicians (22 per group) completed 264 diagnostic cases. The physicians exposed to erroneous LLM suggestions (treatment group) had a mean diagnostic accuracy of 73.3%, representing an adjusted 14.0-percentage-point reduction compared with the control group's 84.9% (95% confidence interval [CI], -18.9 to -9.1; P<0.0001). The top-choice accuracy was 76.1% in the treatment group versus 90.5% in the control group, resulting in an adjusted 18.3-percentage-point difference (95% CI, -26.6 to -10.0). Conclusions: Physicians demonstrate substantial automation bias when exposed to erroneous LLM recommendations, even with voluntary consultation and prior AI literacy training. These findings highlight safety risks that require robust validation frameworks and regulatory safeguards before widespread clinical AI deployment. items.title: International expert consensus on the contemporary role of pelvic exenteration in recurrent or persistent cervical cancer
items.authors: Caruso G, Casaccia Giordano F, Zanagnolo V, et al.
items.abstract: Objective: To evaluate how the role of pelvic exenteration in locally recurrent or persistent cervical cancer has evolved in the era of modern systemic therapies and radiotherapy techniques and to assess the current expert perspectives on patient selection, treatment sequencing, and surgical management. Methods: An international 2-step modified Delphi survey was conducted following a dedicated expert meeting on pelvic exenteration in cervical cancer held at the European Institute of Oncology, Milan, Italy, in October 2025. The faculty members of the scientific meeting were invited to participate in the survey after the presentation and discussion of the available evidence. The questionnaire included 33 statements across 3 domains: (1) patient selection criteria for pelvic exenteration, (2) alternatives to pelvic exenteration, including novel systemic therapies and advanced re-irradiation strategies, and (3) surgical management and reconstructive techniques. Items were rated using a 5-point Likert scale. Consensus was predefined as ≥70% agreement (scores 4-5) or disagreement (scores 1-2). Results: Fifteen experts from 15 different institutions across 5 countries completed the survey. Consensus was achieved for 23 (69.7%) statements. Experts agreed that non-human papillomavirus-associated histologies and high-grade tumors should not be considered contraindications to pelvic exenteration. No specific age or body mass index cut-offs were identified as independently contraindicating surgery, whereas performance status and psychosocial support were deemed essential factors in patient selection. Complete agreement was reached regarding peritoneal dissemination and distant metastatic disease, including para-aortic lymph nodes, as contraindications to pelvic exenteration. The presence of a single positive pelvic lymph node was not generally considered a contraindication to surgery; however, 67% of respondents agreed that the presence of multiple positive pelvic lymph nodes should preclude pelvic exenteration. No consensus was reached regarding non-central disease location, tumor size cut-offs, or the impact of disease timing (persistence versus recurrence). Novel systemic therapies, including immunotherapy and antibody-drug conjugates, were generally preferred over pelvic exenteration unless severe local symptoms, such as fistulas, pelvic pain, and tumor necrosis, required immediate local control.…

items.title: Automated Opportunistic Bone Mineral Density Assessment at Low-Dose CT Lung Cancer Screening: Incident Vertebral Fractures and Mortality
items.authors: Löffler MT, Rühling S, Sollmann N, et al.
items.abstract: Background Low-dose CT (LDCT) for lung cancer screening enables opportunistic volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) assessment, but its prognostic value is unclear. Purpose To evaluate fully automated LDCT-derived vBMD for predicting vertebral fractures and its association with mortality in individuals who heavily smoke. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis included 55-74-year-old individuals who heavily smoked (≥30 pack-years) from the CT arm of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST), a multicenter randomized controlled trial of LDCT versus radiography (participants recruited August 2002 to April 2004). Automated SpineQ software (Bonescreen) was used to measure thoracic and lumbar vBMD (normal, ≥120 mg/cm3; low bone mass [osteopenia], 80 to <120 mg/cm3; osteoporosis, <80 mg/cm3) and vertebral fractures (Genant scale). The outcomes included 1- and 2-year incident vertebral fractures and 6-year mortality (active follow-up to 2009). Poisson and Cox models were adjusted for demographic variables, available comorbidities, and baseline vertebral fractures. Results The NLST included 26 722 participants in the CT arm, with 21 856 included in the present analysis (mean age, 61 years ± 5 [SD]; 12 854 male participants). The 2-year vertebral fracture incidence (n = 18 211 participants with 2-year LDCT) was 0.9% for those with normal bone mass, 2.0% for those with low bone mass (adjusted relative risk, 2.07 [95% CI: 1.70, 2.53]), and 5.9% for those with osteoporosis (adjusted relative risk, 3.40 [95% CI: 2.69, 4.30]). Mortality risk (n = 21 447 participants with completed follow-up [median, 6.65 years]) was associated with osteoporotic vBMD in men (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.24 [95% CI: 1.02, 1.50]). Conclusion Fully automated opportunistic assessment of spinal vBMD predicted vertebral fracture risk and was associated with mortality in men after adjustment. Individuals with osteoporotic vBMD who heavily smoked had a 2-year fracture incidence above the 5% treatment threshold according to current osteoporosis guidelines. Clinical trial registration no. items.title: Angle-Dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm for Fast Proton Therapy Dose Calculations
items.authors: Stryja M, Lathouwers D, Perkó Z
items.abstract: Background: Accurate 3D dose calculation for Pencil Beam Scanning Proton Therapy (PBSPT) is typically performed using Monte Carlo (MC) dose engines. Although MC remains the gold standard for dosimetric accuracy, its high computational cost limits applicability in adaptive workflows and other tasks requiring repeated recalculation. Deep learning methods have recently emerged as a promising alternative for fast and accurate proton dose computation. Purpose And Methods: We address a major limitation of existing deep learning proton dose engines: the requirement that each beamlet be sampled in its beam's-eye-view, with the proton beam direction orthogonal to the lateral image planes, which requires a local beam's-eye-view resampling of the computed tomography (CT) patch for every beamlet. To overcome this, we propose the Angle-dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm (ADoTA), which augments the model with an additional input channel encoding a fast analytical beamlet shape projection. The projection supplies explicit beam direction information so that a single field-level CT transformation remains: the CT is rotated and resampled once per irradiation field to an isotropic 2 × 2 × 2 mm3 grid, and each beamlet is then obtained by cropping the relevant sub-volume from this shared grid. The model was trained on CT data from 108 patients to predict beamlet dose distributions for initial energies from 70 to 150 MeV (thoracic) and 70 to 270 MeV (abdominal/pelvic) over an 80 × 110 mm2 field and evaluated on an independent, non-overlapping test cohort of 50 patients. Results: On the independent test set, ADoTA achieved gamma pass rates of 99.40% ± 0.86% and 99.87% ± 0.23% for thoracic and abdominal/pelvic cases, respectively, under the Γ(1%, 3 mm, 0.1%) criterion. Batched inference achieved an effective throughput equivalent to 3.14 ± 0.31 ms per beamlet at a batch size of 200, whereas a beamlet processed on its own required 14.1 ms. By resampling each field once to a 2 × 2 × 2 mm3 grid and then only cropping the relevant sub-volume per beamlet, ADoTA avoids the beamlet-specific local beam's-eye-view resampling required by prior methods. In a 5640-spot prostate-plan benchmark with both routes optimized on the graphics processing unit (GPU), the analytical beamlet shape projection was 3-4× cheaper on compute and approximately 6-7× cheaper including host-device transfer than batched local beam's-eye-view sampling, per beamlet, reducing the plan's direction-encoding cost by 9.6× and its total compute time by 1.48×.…

items.title: Differentiable Autoplanning Algorithm for Proton Therapy Based on Deep Learning: A Proof-of-Concept
items.authors: Arsini L, Caccia B, Ciardiello A, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: This study presents the proof-of-concept of a novel framework for fully automated proton therapy treatment planning that enables the simultaneous optimization of all major beam parameters, including fluences, energies, and field orientations, within a single differentiable programming approach. The objective is to overcome current limitations of conventional treatment planning systems, which restrict optimization to fluence alone. Materials And Methods: A differentiable deep-learning (DL) dose engine based on Graph Neural Networks was employed to emulate Monte Carlo (MC) dose deposition of proton pencil beams with millisecond inference time and high accuracy. The model predicts energy deposition within a cylindrical scoring volume around each beam, which is subsequently mapped to the CT reference frame using differentiable geometric transformations and interpolation. Exploiting end-to-end differentiability, exact gradients of dose with respect to beam energies, orientations, and fluences were computed and used for plan optimization. A hybrid strategy combining Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA) for global exploration and the Adam gradient-based optimizer for local refinement was implemented. Proof-of-concept evaluations were conducted in homogeneous water phantom geometries and in a head-and-neck phantom CT featuring single- and dual-field configurations targeting a defined planning target volume while sparing organs at risk. Results: The DL dose engine reproduced high-statistics MC simulated dose distributions with mean relative errors of the order of percent, with a computational efficiency compatible with iterative optimization. The joint optimization procedure reliably converged from random initial conditions to reproducible solutions in both single- and dual-field setups, generating clinically meaningful Spread-Out Bragg peaks with homogeneous planning target volume coverage and effective organs at risk sparing. Conclusion: This work demonstrates the feasibility of fully joint, gradient-based optimization of all key proton therapy beam parameters using a differentiable DL dose engine. The proposed framework provides a foundation for next-generation automated treatment planning systems and motivates future extension to patient-specific, clinically realistic scenarios.

items.title: Treatment Effect of Perioperative (Neoadjuvant and Adjuvant) Apalutamide plus Androgen-deprivation Therapy Versus Radical Prostatectomy Alone in Patients with High-risk Localized or Locally Advanced Prostate Cancer from the PROTEUS Substudy
items.authors: Briganti A, Steuber T, Shore ND, et al.
items.abstract: Background: The blinded placebo-controlled PROTEUS (Perioperative Treatment with Erleada United with Surgery) study demonstrated that adding 1-yr perioperative apalutamide plus androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) benefited patients with high-risk localized prostate cancer or locally advanced prostate cancer (HR-LPC/LAPC) who were undergoing radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection (RP). Objective: This substudy evaluated 1-yr perioperative apalutamide plus ADT versus standard-of-care (SOC) RP. Design, Setting, And Participants: Patients with newly diagnosed HR-LPC/LAPC were randomized 1:3 to open-label perioperative apalutamide (240 mg/d) plus ADT (six 28-d cycles before and after RP) or RP. Outcomes Measurements And Statistical Analysis: The primary end point was event-free survival (EFS), defined as time to biochemical failure, local/regional recurrence, distant metastasis, or death. Secondary/other end points included metastasis-free survival (MFS) by conventional or prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography (PSMA PET) imaging, MFS by conventional imaging, and time to first subsequent therapy; p values were nominal. Time-to-event end points were analyzed with the Kaplan-Meier method and stratified Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for the randomization stratification factors to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results And Limitations: In total, 408 patients (median age 66 yr [interquartile range 62-71]) were randomized: perioperative apalutamide plus ADT, n = 102; RP, n = 306. Median follow-up was 37.4 mo in patients without EFS events. Perioperative apalutamide plus ADT significantly improved EFS compared with RP alone (median not reached vs 19.1 mo; estimated 3-yr event-free rates 63% vs 41%; HR 0.38; 95% CI 0.26-0.55; p < 0.001). Because of the nonconstant HR over time, indicating that the proportional hazards assumption was not met, a post hoc restricted mean survival time analysis was performed. This analysis estimated that the average event-free time during the first 36 mo was 31.7 mo (95% CI 30.3-33.1) with perioperative apalutamide plus ADT versus 20.7 mo (95% CI 19.1-22.4) with RP alone, a difference of 11.0 mo (95% CI 8.8-13.1; p < 0.001). MFS by conventional or PSMA PET imaging favored perioperative apalutamide plus ADT over RP alone (estimated 3-yr event-free rates 87% vs 78%; HR 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.90; p = 0.019), and the hazard of subsequent therapy was reduced by 71% (HR 0.29; 95% CI 0.20-0.43; p < 0.001).…

items.title: Anbenitamab plus HB1801 for HER2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer
items.authors: Wang J, Li H, Xu F, et al.
items.abstract: Background: The combination of docetaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) is an established first-line treatment for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive advanced breast cancer. The efficacy and safety of anbenitamab, a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody, plus albumin-bound docetaxel (HB1801) in this context are unknown. Methods: In this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in China, we randomly assigned patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer in a 1:1 ratio to receive either anbenitamab plus HB1801 or THP. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Objective response was a secondary end point. Results: A total of 885 patients were enrolled (445 were assigned to receive anbenitamab plus HB1801 and 440 to receive THP). At this prespecified interim analysis (with 401 events [disease progression or death] and a median follow-up of 21.0 months), the estimated 24-month progression-free survival was significantly higher with anbenitamab plus HB1801 than with THP (58.5% vs. 34.4%; hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.46; 95% confidence interval, 0.37 to 0.56; P<0.001). The percentage of patients with an objective response was 87.6% in the anbenitamab group and 73.4% in the THP group. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 204 of 444 patients (45.9%) in the anbenitamab group and in 151 of 439 patients (34.4%) in the THP group. Neutropenia was the most common adverse event of grade 3 or higher in both groups (13.1% in the anbenitamab group and 8.4% in the THP group). Adverse events leading to death occurred in 2 patients in each group. Conclusions: Anbenitamab plus HB1801 led to significantly higher progression-free survival than THP among patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. (Funded by Shanghai JMT-Bio Technology and others; HEALER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05838066.).

items.title: Sacituzumab Tirumotecan plus Pembrolizumab in PD-L1-Negative Advanced NSCLC
items.authors: Zhou F, Meng X, Ding Q, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal. Methods: In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis. Results: A total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; P<0.001). An objective response occurred in 50.2% and 47.3% of the patients, respectively, and the median duration of response was 13.6 months and 6.8 months. Overall survival data were immature; the hazard ratio for death was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.88). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that occurred after the start of treatment were reported in 47.6% of the patients assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab and in 60.6% of those assigned to receive chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Stomatitis was common with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab, but the events were predominantly grade 1 or 2. Conclusions: Among patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. (Funded by Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical; OptiTROP-Lung06 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06711900.).

items.title: Osimertinib-Savolitinib in Advanced NSCLC after Progression during EGFR-TKI Therapy
items.authors: Lu S, Girard N, Yang JC, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy. Methods: In this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety. Results: Of the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; P<0.001), as well as significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.91; P = 0.01; final analysis). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of 12-month progression-free survival was 36% in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and 10% in the platinum-pemetrexed group, and the estimate of 12-month overall survival was 70% and 53%, respectively. The most frequently reported adverse events that occurred during treatment in the osimertinib-savolitinib group were peripheral edema (in 49% of the patients), anemia (in 26%), and diarrhea (in 26%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group. Conclusions: Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

items.title: Efficacy and safety of risvutatug rezetecan versus gemcitabine plus docetaxel in relapsed/refractory advanced osteosarcoma: Primary results from the ARTEMIS-011 phase 3 trial
items.authors: Xie L, Yao W, Hua Y, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) osteosarcoma have a poor prognosis and high unmet needs for effective therapies. Herein, we report primary results from ARTEMIS-011, the multicenter, open-label, randomized phase 3 trial of risvutatug rezetecan (Ris-Rez), a B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugate, in Chinese patients with R/R osteosarcoma after ≥2 prior lines of systemic treatment. Patients And Methods: Patients (≥12 years) were randomized 2:1 to Ris-Rez 12.0 mg/kg or gemcitabine plus docetaxel (GD), every 3 weeks, stratified by age and lung metastasis. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review (BICR); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS) and safety. Results: At data cutoff (June 17, 2026), 80 patients were treated with Ris-Rez and 42 with GD; median follow-up was 7.1 months. Median age was 21 years (IQR, 17-34) with 31 (25%) adolescents (12 to <18 years). BICR-assessed PFS significantly improved with Ris-Rez compared with GD (median, 5.5 vs 1.4 months; HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.20-0.55; P<0.0001). OS data were immature, with a HR of 0.51 (95% CI, 0.21-1.23). With longer treatment duration with Ris-Rez than GD (median, 4.5 vs 1.5 months), adverse events (AEs) were reported in all patients. No treatment-related AEs (TRAEs) led to death. Grade ≥ 3 TRAEs occurred in 93% of patients with Ris-Rez and 83% with GD, and serious TRAEs in 64% versus 29%, which were predominantly hematologic. TRAEs led to dose reductions in 71% versus 26% of patients with Ris-Rez versus GD, respectively, and permanent discontinuation was infrequent (3.8% vs 2.4%). Conclusions: In ARTEMIS-011, Ris-Rez demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in BICR-assessed PFS compared to GD, alongside a numerical trend toward improved OS and manageable safety profile with dose modifications and supportive care, offering a promising new treatment option for patients with R/R advanced osteosarcoma.

items.title: Final analysis of the Neotorch study: perioperative toripalimab in combination with chemotherapy for patients with stage Ⅱ/Ⅲ resectable non-small-cell lung cancer
items.authors: Li ZM, Wu L, Wang WX, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Interim analysis of the Neotorch study demonstrated significant benefit in event-free survival (EFS) and major pathological response (MPR) rate for perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable stage Ⅲ non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In this article, we report the overall final analysis results of the stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ patients in this study. Patients And Methods: Eligible patients with treatment-naïve resectable stage II or stage IIIA, IIIB (N2) NSCLC were randomly assigned to receive toripalimab or placebo plus chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment (three cycles), adjuvant treatment (one cycle), and toripalimab or placebo monotherapy as maintenance treatment (up to 13 cycles). The primary endpoints of this study were EFS assessed by investigators and MPR evaluated by blinded independent pathologic review in stage Ⅲ patients, as well as the overall outcome in stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ patients. Results: A total of 501 patients in China were included in this randomized study (toripalimab arm: N = 250, placebo arm: N = 251). Baseline characteristics were generally balanced between the 2 arms. At the final analysis (median follow-up of 48.2 months), the investigator-assessed EFS was significantly improved in the toripalimab arm, with a stratified hazard ratio (HR) of 0.52 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.39-0.68, stratified P < 0.0001]. The median EFS in the toripalimab arm was not reached, while it was 20.2 months in the placebo arm. The between-arm difference in MPR rate was statistically significant and clinically meaningful (47% compared with 9%, P < 0.0001). Overall survival (OS) prolongation was also statistically significant in the toripalimab arm (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.49-0.89, P = 0.0072), with median survival not reached in either arm. The safety profile was consistent with that of the interim analysis, with no new safety signals identified. Conclusions: Perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy demonstrated durable and significant benefits in EFS, MPR, and OS in patients with resectable stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ NSCLC, with a manageable safety profile. items.title: Prospective circulating tumour DNA surveillance in patients with early high-risk hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in the TRAK-ER study
items.authors: Cunningham N, Swift C, Cutts RJ, et al.
items.abstract: Background: CtDNA detection during adjuvant endocrine therapy (ET) strongly associates with recurrence in oestrogen receptor (ER) positive early breast cancer (EBC), with potential to direct switches in adjuvant treatment. Patients And Methods: TRAK-ER is a multicentre study for patients with high-risk, ER-positive, HER2-negative EBC, who undergo 3 monthly ctDNA surveillance for up to 3 years during adjuvant ET. High-risk included ≥4 involved lymph nodes; tumour >5 cm; 1-3 involved lymph nodes with additional high-risk features. Upon ctDNA detection, patients have staging scans and in the absence of radiological recurrence, are randomised to receive palbociclib plus fulvestrant or standard ET. ctDNA analysis was performed using a tumour informed assay (Labcorp). We report a protocol-specified analysis of ctDNA detection during surveillance, and results of contemporaneous radiological recurrence. Results: 1133 patients were registered by September 2025, 928 had panels designed (design failed in 16.1% (178/1106), and 912 started ctDNA surveillance including results from 5810 tests (median 7 per patient). ctDNA detection rate was 5.0% (45/897) in the first test, and 1.3% (66/4913) in subsequent tests (P<0.001). Patient level detection rate was 12.0% (109/912), with 1.1% (10/912) of patients having a clinical recurrence without prior ctDNA detection. Detection positively associated with nodal burden (P<0.001) and grade (P=0.04) and negatively associated with increasing time from surgery (P=0.01). Estimated cumulative ctDNA detection rate at 5 years post-surgery was 23.7% (95%CI 14.5-31.9%). In patients with ctDNA detected on the first test, 65.9% (29/44) had radiological recurrence compared to 26.6% (17/64) in patients first detected on subsequent tests (P<0.001). Conclusion: Results from TRAK-ER inform implementation of ctDNA surveillance in ER-positive EBC, including molecular relapse rates, factors associating with ctDNA detection and contemporaneous radiological recurrence. Ultrasensitive assays detecting ctDNA at low levels, are required to robustly identify patients prior to clinical recurrence. TRAK-ER is ongoing to assess the impact of treatment after molecular relapse detection.

items.title: A cascade deep learning network for simultaneous prediction of dose and linear energy transfer in proton therapy of prostate cancer
items.authors: Liu Q, Wei S, Peng H, et al.
items.abstract: Objective: Prediction of dose-averaged linear energy transfer (LETd) may facilitate LET-aware evaluation of proton therapy plans. This study developed a cascade deep learning framework for simultaneous three-dimensional prediction of dose and LETd distributions for conventional dose-based optimization (DoseOpt) and LETd-incorporated optimization (LETOpt) in prostate intensity-modulated proton therapy. Approach: A total of 150 patients with prostate cancer were included, each with DoseOpt and LETOpt plans. Planning CT images and anatomical structure masks were used as inputs. The cascade network transferred an intermediate latent representation from the dose prediction pathway to the LETd prediction pathway. Stepwise, multitask, and anatomy-only LETd (only-LET) networks served as comparators. Model performance was evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. Main Results: All dose-predicting models showed high spatial agreement, with cascade Dice similarity coefficients of approximately 0.93, 0.96, and 0.95 for the 50%, 75%, and 95% prescription isodose volumes. No significant differences in structure-specific dose errors remained after false discovery rate correction. The cascade model achieved the lowest global LETd MAE for DoseOpt and LETOpt, 0.108 ± 0.025 and 0.111 ± 0.025 keV/μm, respectively, significantly lower than those of the multitask, stepwise, and only-LET models. Structure-specific LETd performance was endpoint dependent, with favorable cascade performance for several CTV and organ-at-risk endpoints. LETOpt primarily redistributed LETd while largely preserving dose, and the cascade model reproduced the principal plan-specific changes, including reductions in rectal and rectal-wall LETd. Mean inference time was 0.505 ± 0.020 s per patient. Significance: The proposed framework enables rapid simultaneous prediction of dose and LETd for predefined planning strategies from patient anatomy without requiring a precomputed dose distribution, supporting LET-aware plan comparison and providing a basis for future LETd-guided biological optimization.

items.title: Resident training in brachytherapy in France: A 15-year update after the first survey of SFjRO members
items.authors: Houdou L, Raynaud C, Evin C, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Brachytherapy requires dedicated procedural expertise and sustained supervised exposure. After national surveys in 2012 and 2021, we reassessed training among French radiation oncology residents in 2026, using a harmonized, individual-level repeated cross-sectional comparison to examine 15-year trends. Methods And Materials: An anonymous questionnaire was distributed at the March 2026 national brachytherapy course of the French Society of Young Radiation Oncologists and the National College of Teachers in Radiation Oncology; items came from previous surveys to preserve comparability. Proportions are given with 95% confidence intervals (CI); 2021 and 2026 individual-level data were compared with chi-square or Fisher exact tests, and three-survey trends with the Cochran-Armitage test. Results: Of 200 registered residents, 146 responded (73.0%). Brachytherapy represented under 10% of residency for 86.3%, training was considered insufficient by 80.8%, unchanged since 2012 (81.5%) and 2021 (79.7%; P for trend 0.948), and only 24.0% felt able or rather able to practise autonomously. No technique gained in independent performance over 15 years, while declared interest fell from 91.3% (2012) to 86.4% (2021) and 63.7% (2026; P for trend <0.001). Logistic barriers collapsed between 2021 and 2026 (rotating through several centres 84.7% to 17.8%, P<0.001), whereas insufficient exposure rose (50.0% to 70.5%, P<0.001), low academic recognition (51.4%) and lack of mentors (46.6%) becoming the leading barriers. Autonomy rose across the curriculum but stayed low (9.1% to 32.4%; P for trend 0.024), and 10.8% of end-of-curriculum residents had never had any brachytherapy rotation. Conclusion: Brachytherapy training in France remains characterized by limited hands-on exposure, low autonomy and persistent structural barriers, and resident interest appears to be declining. The barriers appear to have shifted from logistic obstacles, now largely resolved, toward structural and human ones: lack of protected time, mentorship and academic recognition, calling for protected rotations in expert centers, inter-hospital mobility, mentorship and simulation-based teaching.

items.title: Subgroup variations in benefit from telehealth palliative care for advanced lung cancer
items.authors: Post KE, Trotter CS, Munankarmi AM, et al.
items.abstract: We examined whether the impact on quality of life (QOL) of early palliative care delivered via video versus in-person visits varied across patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Between 6/2018 and 5/2023, 1250 patients with advanced NSCLC enrolled in a randomized trial comparing early palliative care delivered via video or in-person visits at 22 cancer centers. Using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Lung scale, we examined whether the effect of palliative care delivery modality on patient-reported QOL at 24 weeks post-enrollment varied by baseline sociodemographic and other factors. Black patients, Hispanic/Latino patients, and those with incomes <$50,000 reported better QOL in the video visit group versus the in-person group. However, Asian patients in the video visit group reported worse QOL than the in-person group. Early palliative care delivered via video may provide greater QOL benefits for Black and Hispanic/Latino patients with advanced NSCLC and those with lower incomes. Trial Registration: NCT03375489.

items.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Lenalidomide-Dexamethasone in Combination With Radiotherapy in Solitary Plasmacytoma
items.journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
items.authors: Loap P, Laroze S, Bouscary D, et al.
items.abstract: Introduction: Radiotherapy achieves excellent local control in solitary plasmacytoma, but systemic progression remains a major limitation. We evaluated the long-term association between lenalidomide-dexamethasone combined with radiotherapy and disease outcomes. Materials And Methods: This retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database included 75 consecutive patients with solitary plasmacytoma treated between 2004 and 2025. All patients underwent bone marrow assessment, serum free light-chain testing, and magnetic resonance imaging, with PET/CT routinely incorporated into staging from late 2008 onward. Patients received radiotherapy alone (n=42) or radiotherapy combined with lenalidomide-dexamethasone (n=33). Primary endpoints were progression-free survival and multiple myeloma-free survival. Systemic progression-free survival, defined by progression to multiple myeloma, multiple plasmacytomas, or distant solitary plasmacytoma, was additionally evaluated. Results: Median follow-up was 6.31 years. Only three local recurrences occurred. Lenalidomide-dexamethasone was associated with longer progression-free survival (HR, 0.315; 95% CI, 0.128-0.775; p=0.012), with 10-year rates of 71.8% versus 26.7% after radiotherapy alone. Among the six patients progressing after combined treatment, three (50.0%) developed multiple myeloma and three (50.0%) developed multiple plasmacytomas. Multiple myeloma-free survival did not differ significantly between groups (10-year rates, 86.6% vs 65.9%; p=0.19). Conclusion: Lenalidomide-dexamethasone combined with radiotherapy was associated with sustained improvement in progression-free survival in solitary plasmacytoma. These long-term findings support prospective evaluation of upfront lenalidomide-dexamethasone in combination with radiotherapy for solitary plasmacytoma.

items.title: P047-1 Pembrolizumab plus trastuzumab as frontline therapy in HER2-positive gastric cancer: a systematic review
items.authors: R.D. Sidabutar, M. A.w Hutapea
items.abstract: Gastric cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality, with limited survival in advanced disease despite chemotherapy. About 20-30% of gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancers are HER2-positive, where trastuzumab plus chemotherapy is standard. Immunotherapy targeting PD-1/PD-L1 has shown benefit. The KEYNOTE-811 trial demonstrated that adding pembrolizumab improved response rates and progression-free survival, especially in PD-L1 CPS ≥1 tumors, leading to FDA approval in 2025. However, questions remain regarding long-term outcomes, safety, and biomarker-driven selection.

items.authors: S. Kadowaki, Y. Ishizuka, H. Taniguchi, N. Kiyota, S. Okano, Y. Shimizu, M. Kobara, C. Kudo, M. Ando, K. Mori, K. Muro
items.abstract: Salivary gland cancer (SGC) is a rare malignancy, accounting for approximately 0.3% of all cancers. In patients without actionable molecular alterations, platinum-based chemotherapy remains standard, although efficacy is limited. Angiogenic pathway activation is frequently observed in SGC subtypes, supporting the rationale for anti-angiogenic therapy. Fruquintinib, an oral VEGFR-1, -2, and -3 inhibitor, may have therapeutic potential in SGC. However, the rarity of the disease hampers further development.

items.abstract: The combination of locoregional and system therapies for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) is gaining broader acceptance following multiple positive phase III randomized controlled trials. The combination of immune checkpoint inhibitors and VEGF inhibitors have shown particular promise. However, most studies focus on the additive effects of systemic therapies to trans-arterial chemoembolization (TACE) rather than vice versa. This study investigated the impact of TACE with non-curative intent (“add-on TACE”) during the course of atezolizumab + bevacizumab therapy (AB) on clinical outcomes in uHCC.

items.title: Impact of tissue heterogeneity on intracranial Cesium-131 brachytherapy dosimetry: A patient-specific Monte Carlo Study
items.authors: Adhikari T, Jung JW, Gadoue SM, et al.
items.abstract: Background: AAPM TG-43-based dose calculations for intracranial cesium-131 (131Cs) brachytherapy ignore patient-specific heterogeneities, which can affect dose accuracy. This study investigates the dosimetric impact of these heterogeneity effects using Monte Carlo (MC) simulations and patient-specific imaging data. Purpose: To quantify the impact of tissue heterogeneity on dose distributions in intracranial brachytherapy using 131Cs sources and to evaluate the accuracy of AAPM TG-43-based treatment planning system (TPS) calculations. Methods: TG-43 dosimetric parameters for the 131Cs source were independently characterized and benchmarked against published consensus data. MC simulations using MCNP were performed in both homogeneous water phantoms and heterogeneous voxelized lattice phantoms derived from CT DICOM RT data. Single and multiple-seed configurations were investigated. TPS and MC dose distributions were compared using dose-volume histogram (DVH) metrics such as (V60, V100, D2cc, and mean dose), isodose distributions, dose difference maps, and local and global dose difference analyzes. Spatial agreement was quantified using gamma analysis. Results: Strong agreement was observed between TPS and MC calculations in homogeneous media. However, heterogeneous patient-specific MC simulations revealed systematic differences in DVH metrics for the target volume and organs at risk, including the skull and skin. Local dose differences revealed pronounced deviations near high-density bony regions, where dose enhancement effects were observed, while global dose difference analyzes demonstrated an overall dosimetric bias. Gamma pass rates decreased in heterogeneous regions, consistent with these spatial dose discrepancies. Compared with the MC simulations, the TG-43-based TPS overestimated the mean dose to the target by approximately 23.63 ± 4.97  %  , V60 and V100 by approximately 24.42 ± 4.97  %  , and 23.75 ± 4.97  %  , respectively, and the mean dose to the skin by approximately 73.60 ± 4.97  %  , while underestimating the mean dose to the skull by 220.90 ± 4.97  %  . Conclusion: Although the TG-43 formalism provides accurate dose estimates in homogeneous media, it introduces clinically meaningful local and global dosimetric deviations in heterogeneous intracranial environments.…

items.title: Vision and implementation for the first U.S. carbon ion therapy center part I: Clinical rationale and the need for CIRT in the United States
items.authors: Liang X, Beltran CJ
items.abstract: Carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) has evolved into an established clinical modality over the past three decades. Owing to its unique physical and biological characteristics, CIRT has demonstrated favorable outcomes for selected malignancies characterized by radioresistance, proximity to critical organs, locally advanced disease requiring safe dose escalation, and recurrent tumors requiring re-irradiation. This review summarizes the physical and radiobiological rationale for CIRT, the evolution of international clinical practice and the clinical relative biological effectiveness models and dose prescription systems currently used in Asia and Europe. We discuss the differences between the modified microdosimetric kinetic model and Local Effect Model frameworks and their implications for interpreting and applying international clinical experience. We also describe the biological dose calculation framework adopted by Mayo Clinic Florida (MCF) to integrate established international CIRT experience into the first U.S. program. Published estimates of CIRT eligibility and need in the United States are reviewed to provide context for the anticipated U.S. patient population. This population includes many clinically complex disease sites characterized by proximity to critical organs, respiratory motion, anatomical variation, and the potential need for adaptive treatment. These clinical characteristics define important requirements for the first U.S. CIRT program and provide the foundation for the design philosophy and technical implementation described in the companion Part II article.

items.title: Long-Term Outcomes of a Prospective Study on Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Guided Whole-Gland Salvage High-Dose-Rate Prostate Brachytherapy for Locally Recurrent Prostate Cancer
items.authors: Hu HP, Morton G, Loblaw A, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Whole-gland salvage high-dose-rate (HDR) prostate brachytherapy is an emerging option for radiorecurrent prostate cancer. However, long-term prospective data remain limited. This report presents the long-term results of our prospective study on the toxicities, health-related quality of life, and efficacy of whole-gland HDR prostate brachytherapy. Methods And Materials: Patients with biopsy-confirmed, magnetic resonance (MR)-visible local recurrent prostate cancer after previous external beam radiation therapy (EBRT) were eligible. Patients underwent MR-assisted, ultrasound-based whole-gland HDR prostate brachytherapy with a prescription dose of 21 Gy to the entire prostate and 27 Gy to the MR-defined intraprostatic target volume (TV) divided over 2 implants separated by 1 to 2 weeks. Adjuvant androgen deprivation therapy was not used. Results: Thirty patients were enrolled in the study. Median follow-up from salvage HDR was 72.0 months (10.7-121.5 months). Most patients (93%) had initial EBRT doses at conventional fractionation. The pre-HDR median prostate-specific antigen was 3.67 ng/mL (0.56-11.01 ng/mL). Seven (23.3%) were staged with prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography. Four (13%) required temporary urinary catheterization. There was only 1 (3.3%) grade 3 to 5 toxicity-a late grade 3 genitourinary toxicity. The prostate-specific antigen progression-free survival and freedom from androgen deprivation therapy rates were 73.0% and 93.0% at 3 years, and 24.8% and 69.6% at 5 years, respectively. Of the 26 patients who had a post-HDR MR imaging (median, 415 days), 9 (35%) had persistent disease. Of the 23 (77%) patients who had prostate-specific antigen relapse, 18 (78%) patients had disease at the TV confirmed by MR imaging, prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography, or targeted biopsy. Conclusions: Whole-gland salvage HDR brachytherapy with intraprostatic boost is well tolerated. Progression after salvage treatment was associated with local failure.

items.title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial
items.authors: George S, Vaishampayan U, Hutson A, et al.
items.abstract: Background: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls. Methods: In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants. Findings: Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories.…
